list.name: testid
list.label: Test
list.query: SHOW TAG VALUES FROM "http_req_duration" WITH KEY = "testid"

list.name: build
list.label: Build
list.query: SHOW TAG VALUES FROM "http_req_duration" WITH KEY = "build" WHERE "testid" =~ /^$testid$/

list.name: level
list.label: Concurrency
list.query: SHOW TAG VALUES FROM "http_req_duration" WITH KEY = "level" WHERE "testid" =~ /^$testid$/

title: k6 CRM Load Tests - Latency, Build Trend & Bottlenecks

panels.title: Goal 1 - p95 by concurrency - $testid (build $build)
panels.description: How latency (p95) scales as concurrent users go 10 -> 30 -> 50 -> 100. One panel per test (repeats over $testid), each auto-scaled. Teardown/cleanup requests (no level tag) are excluded.

targets.query: SELECT percentile("value", 95) FROM "http_req_duration" WHERE "testid" =~ /^$testid$/ AND "build" =~ /^$build$/ AND "level" =~ /^($level)$/ AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "level" fill(none)

panels.title: Error rate by concurrency - $testid (build $build)
panels.description: http_req_failed averaged per level -> % of failed HTTP requests at each concurrency. Should stay ~0%. One panel per test.

targets.query: SELECT mean("value") * 100 AS "error_pct" FROM "http_req_failed" WHERE "testid" =~ /^$testid$/ AND "build" =~ /^$build$/ AND "level" =~ /^($level)$/ AND $timeFilter GROUP BY "level"

panels.title: Goal 2 - p95 trend across builds - $testid
panels.description: Each cluster of points = one build/run over calendar time (time order = build order). Rising over time = regression vs the earlier baseline. Widen the time range (top-right) to see more history. One panel per test (auto-scaled).

targets.query: SELECT percentile("value", 95) FROM "http_req_duration" WHERE "testid" =~ /^$testid$/ AND "level" =~ /^($level)$/ AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "level" fill(null)

panels.title: Goal 3 - Bottleneck: latency by operation - $testid (build $build)
panels.description: http_req_duration broken down by concurrency level and by operation tag (step=get/post for login; rpc=create/search/unlink for create-lead) plus the URL (name). Sorted by p95 descending -> the slowest operation is at the top. One panel per test.

targets.query: SELECT mean("value") AS "avg_ms", percentile("value", 95) AS "p95_ms", max("value") AS "max_ms", count("value") AS "reqs" FROM "http_req_duration" WHERE "testid" =~ /^$testid$/ AND "build" =~ /^$build$/ AND $timeFilter GROUP BY "level", "step", "rpc"

options.content:
### Create-lead - the bottleneck  (latency / scaling risk, 0 failures)
- **Risk** - create() p95 = **15.1 s** at 100 concurrent users (**75%** of the 20 s gate); scales **~5.5x** from 10 -> 100 users, so ~130-140 concurrent creates would breach the gate. Lead intake is the first thing to buckle under a spike.
- **Cause** - create() is **serialized**, not compute-bound: latency grows with *concurrency* (requests queue), not payload - the signature of a shared serial resource (Odoo's synchronous lead assignment / scoring + row locks on each new lead).
- **Evidence** - on the *same* new leads, a `search` returns in **0.68 s** avg but a `delete` (`unlink`) **blocks up to 121 s** (avg **62.7 s**, p95 **92 s**). Fast read + stalled write on identical rows = they are **lock-held by the assignment cron** - the same contention that inflates create() under load. (Deletes are cleanup-only, so they never fail the test - but they are the clearest fingerprint of the lock.)

### Login - healthy
p95 stays **< 1 s** even at 100 users and scales **sub-linearly** (2.2x for a 10x user increase). Heavier half is the initial `GET /web/login` CSRF page (p95 1.14 s) vs the auth `POST` (0.95 s) - a static-asset detail, not a scaling concern.

_Baseline: login #2, create-lead #6. All requests succeeded - this is a latency/scaling risk, not a functional defect. Watch create() p95 @ 100u build-over-build._
